To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Mn-SOD gene plays a role in vascular function.
the Mn-SOD gene is a major regulator of the function of resistance arteries.

a decrease in mitochondrial manganese-superoxidodismutase (MnSOD) leads to increased vascular oxidative stress and a decrease in endothelial nitic oxide synthase (NOS) activity, resulting in impaired vasodilatation in isolated mesenteri arteries of mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of superoxide in endothelium-dependent vasodilations in resistance arteries of wild-type (WT), Mn-SOD+(-), and Mn-SOD-(-/-) mice.
the role of superoxide in the regulation of blood flow in the vascular system.
the effects of superoxide on vascular function in isolated mesenterie arteries from Mn-SOD+ and wild-type mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the lack of Mn-SOD in the vascular wall results in a decrease in the bioavailability of nitric oxide, which is responsible for the decrease in flow-induced dilation in the Mn-SOD-deficiency mouse model.

the lack of mitochondrial MnSOD in mice leads to a significant increase in superoxide production in vascular tissue, which leads to decreased flow-, acetylcholine-, and sodium nitroprussside-induced dilations in resistance arteries and to decreased nitric oxide synthases activity.
a decrease in the activity of Mn-SODE leads to a reduction in the vasodilator response to flow and to agonists.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MnSOD is an essential enzyme for the maintenance of vascular tone and function.
Mn-SOD deficiency results in increased superoxide, which inactivating nitric oxide and decreasing endothelial nitric synthase activity leads to impaired vasodilatory response.
Mn-SOD is a critical component of vascular function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
superoxide, which is a free radical, is a major player in the pathogenesis of vascular dysfunction.
Mn-SOD is an important antioxidant in the vasculature.
the loss of Mn-SOD leads to an increase in superoxide, which inactivating nitric oxide and reducing eNOS activity contributes to the impaired vascular function of Mn-SOD knockout mice.
